attacks.claim: In dark mode `.day-card` keeps a hardcoded white background while its text switches to near-white, so card text and muted meta text are nearly unreadable for the roughly 30% of users on dark mode. The app has supported dark mode since v5, so this is a regression.

The fixed 72px action bar overlaps the bottom of `.planner`, and no bottom padding reserves space for it. Sunday's day card, its Swap and overflow buttons, and any focused control scrolled beneath the bar can be obscured and unreachable.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } with .planner { ... padding: 16px; } and "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The tile image has a 320px width attribute and no CSS constraint. On 360px phones the content width is about 296px, so the image overflows the card and causes horizontal scroll or clipping. 360px is the most common mobile width in the stated usage.
attacks.evidence: with no img rule in planner.css

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action (9.4 shopping-list adds per user per week, 64% on mobile) went from one tap to a six-step path after the tile-level "+ List" button was removed. The artifact does not justify or measure this against the clutter goal, and offers no per-recipe or per-day add control.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." and "tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → \"Add to list\" → toast with \"Undo\""; ABSENT: any per-recipe or per-day add control on the tile or day card

attacks.claim: The server-side actions (bulk "Generate shopping list", drag-to-move, "Share plan") have no specified failure behavior. Nothing covers partial failure, retries, idempotency on duplicate bulk adds, undo for the bulk path, optimistic-update rollback, or user-visible error states, so the UI and stored plan can diverge silently.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) and "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." ABSENT: error, partial-failure, retry, rollback, or undo behavior for these actions

attacks.claim: Observability and rollback criteria are insufficient for a 100% launch. There are no alert thresholds, no rollback trigger, no baseline for bounce rate or list additions, no alert routing, no named owner for the launch window, and no metrics for the new bulk, move, or share actions.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate." ABSENT: thresholds, alert routing, rollback criteria, owner for the Tuesday 10:00 PT window

attacks.claim: The rollout goes to 100% of web users at once, with no staged ramp or canary. The flag provides a fallback, but a regression in a core flow would reach all mobile and dark-mode users before anyone can detect it.

QA covers only light mode at two widths (Chrome 1440px and iPhone 14), and only happy paths. Dark mode, the 360px Android width carrying most traffic, API errors, slow or offline networks, and empty weeks were never verified, which is where the blockers above appear.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%." ABSENT: dark-mode, 360px, failure-path, or offline QA

attacks.claim: The "Undo" toast after adding to the shopping list has no stated live-region announcement, so screen-reader users may not learn the add succeeded or that Undo is available. Its duration is also unspecified, which matters for users who need more time.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: aria-live/role=status for the toast; "toast with 'Undo'" with no duration stated

attacks.claim: Rollback is asserted as safe ("same API, no data migration"), but nothing confirms that v7-written plans are readable by the v6 planner. Flipping the flag off after users save under v7 is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)." ABSENT: confirmation that v7 writes are readable by the v6 planner
